Bobox — UI overhaul

A full rebuild of the interface of my file-sharing app: from 2023 Material UI defaults to a custom shadcn/Tailwind design system — same backend, new everything else.

React + Tailwind + shadcn/ui Light & dark mode Mobile-first (390px ✓) Long-press & right-click menus Fluid animations In-app file previews New logo ~40% lighter bundle Fully responsive

Login — first impression

Same navy, same layout idea, but the new card is calmer: real tabs, inline icons, a proper Google button, and a design that breathes on phones.

Sign up

The old form crams six fields in a plain white box. The new one adds password strength feedback, labelled inputs, and a friendly switch.

File browser — the heart of the app

Same files, new structure: tidy rows with colour-coded icons, per-item menus, search and filters that fit the width. Dark mode was never a second-class citizen.

File browser — on the phone

The old list keeps desktop paddings and two floating action buttons. The new one is built for thumbs: full-width rows, a sticky action bar, one-hand reach.

Uploads

From a bare browser file input to a drag-and-drop zone with a big target, size label, and one clear Upload button.

File page

Same information, calmer card, and a Preview button that opens the file inside Bobox instead of only images in a popup.

In-app previews (new feature)

The old app could only show images in a plain popup. Now images, video, audio, PDFs and text/code files all open inside a proper dialog — with a Download button.

Account page

The old page crashed on open (a one-line router bug from 2023). The new one shows an avatar, storage usage, and a clean logout.

404

From two silent lines of text to a real page that gets you home.

The 3-dots menu — invisible taps, fixed

Tapping the dots appeared to do nothing: the menu was opening off-screen because React 18 silently dropped Radix's anchor ref. Upgrading to React 19 anchored every popup.

Context gestures (new feature)

The native way to get the actions menu: hold a row for half a second on touch — it dims, buzzes once, and the menu opens without the row navigating. On desktop, right-click opens the same menu. The dots button stays for quick taps.

Motion polish (new)

Pages fade-rise in on navigation, rows cascade in with a 45ms stagger (screenshot caught mid-flight), tab panels animate on switch, and every popup has eased entrance. Transform/opacity only — 60fps on phones, and fully disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

Move-to-folder picker — rebuilt

The old picker asked for double-clicks to open folders and a separate selection tap — nearly impossible on a phone, and it showed only the current folder's name. The new one is a real folder browser: tap to open, a clickable breadcrumb for the full path, and the button names the exact destination. It renders one depth at a time from the client cache, and says "Already in this folder" when it can't move.

Colour palette — steel blue → calm sage

The overhaul started on the inherited MUI steel-blue. It worked, but it felt corporate and the blues fought each other. The new palette is a green-teal system: sage primary, warm neutral backgrounds, teal/olive/amber/coral for file types — friendlier, and every icon colour now has room to breathe. Swapping it was a pure token change: 2 CSS blocks, zero component edits.

Logo — from stock navy box to sage tile

The 2023 logo was a navy/amber isometric box — great shape, colors of a theme that no longer exists. The new one keeps the isometric box, regenerated in the calm-sage palette (AI-assisted concepts, hand-picked), with clean transparent corners for every icon size: navbar, favicons, Android and iOS home screens.

Built by Ofek — one weekend, one agent, zero MUI left.
